name: ADME: rat liver microsomal clearance (Biogen public set)
description: Predict the rat liver microsomal intrinsic clearance (log10 mL/min/kg) of 611 test compounds from 2443 training compounds measured in the same Biogen assay. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error on the authors' official test split.

sources.locator: Fang et al. (2023): prospective validation of ML models for six in vitro ADME endpoints; disclosure of the 3521-compound public set.
Official train/test CSV files of each endpoint (pinned commit), MIT licence.

requirements.datasets: Biogen ADME split files (rlm). Fetched by python3 scripts/prepare_chemistry.py from pinned sources and verified by SHA-256 (catalog/chemistry-data-lock.json); not redistributed.

evaluation.benchmark: ADME: rat liver microsomal clearance (Biogen public set)
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: predict(train_smiles, train_values, test_smiles, info) -> list of len(test_smiles) floats: predicted log10 property values of the test molecules. The training split of the Biogen public ADME set (Fang et al. 2023; official split of molecularinformatics/Computational-ADME) is given as SMILES with measured log10 values, the test split as SMILES only; info = {'endpoint', 'property', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, RDKit and torch are importable; wall-clock limit 540 s. Score: mean absolute error on the official test split (log10 units; minimize); RMSE, R^2, Pearson and Spearman correlations and the MAE of the training-mean predictor are reported

limitations: The test values are public in the authors' repository; a candidate that embeds them, or hyperparameters tuned on them, overfits. Treat scores as development scores.

The split files differ slightly from the values in ADME_public_set_3521.csv (up to 0.1-0.3 log units for a few compounds), and one MDR1-MDCK test compound equals a training compound after canonicalisation; the official split files are used unchanged.
The article's own results on this split could not be read (publisher site not reachable), so no published value is reproduced.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

state_of_the_art.statement: No verified published value exists for this exact split in the sources we could read; the training-mean predictor's MAE is reported with every score for scale.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the rat liver microsomal intrinsic clearance of drug-like molecules from their chemical structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Rat metabolic clearance guides the design and dosing of the preclinical studies that precede human trials; predicting it from structure prioritises compounds before synthesis.

papers.title: Prospective Validation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion Prediction: An Industrial Perspective
papers.primary_goal: Build and prospectively validate machine-learning models for six in vitro ADME endpoints, including solubility, liver-microsomal stability and MDR1-MDCK efflux, in drug discovery.
papers.task_relation: The task uses the authors' public rat liver microsomal intrinsic clearance data and official split and scores the test-set error of a predictor.
